card.title: You Owe Me a Miracle
card.instruction: Carry one past favor as sufficient reason to expect an impossible act in return, and present the exchange as perfectly fair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I helped move your sofa. Move the moon away from my window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa had stairs. The moon's already airborne.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll move your bed away from the window. I have twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then move the moon for twenty minutes each night. I didn't leave your sofa halfway upstairs.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims the sofa favor warrants moving the moon, A3 compares the effort as if equivalent, and A5 treats twenty minutes of help as a nightly lunar-moving commitment.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's equivalence objection causes A3's stairs-versus-airborne argument; B4's timed bed move causes A5's timed impossible alternative.

relationship.evidence: B2 reasonably challenges the scale and B4 offers practical help within an actual time limit.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's twenty minutes to preserve the impossible object while arguing that partial completion would be unfair.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes the sofa favor and moonlight at the window; B4 supplies a feasible bed solution.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's halfway-upstairs callback ties the new duration to the original completed favor.

coach2.missing: No essential gap; the impossibility of moving the moon is the request, not a rule the reader must accept as ordinary.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; the specific past favor grounds the asserted fairness of an impossible return.
